title: Lesson 3.6 — Phonics, Structured Literacy, and Orthographic Mapping
source: User-provided WGU D669 lesson and uploaded Orthographic Mapping transcript
overview: Phonics teaches correspondences between phonemes (sounds) and graphemes (letters or letter patterns). Explicit, systematic, cumulative, diagnostic instruction supports decoding and spelling and increasingly complex word patterns.
learning_objective: Explain phonics instruction and how systematic instruction helps students develop decoding skills.

concepts.description: How written letters and patterns correspond to speech sounds.
Explicit, systematic, cumulative, and diagnostic literacy instruction.
Forming connections among a word's phonemes, graphemes and meaning for accurate automatic word recognition.
Breaking longer words into syllables and meaningful parts and checking the decoded result.

structured_literacy_components.meaning: Planned progression from simpler to more complex skills
Practice and review that builds on previous learning
Use checks and feedback to guide targeted instruction

structured_lesson_sequence: Review prior short-vowel learning with word cards
State objective for short vowel graphemes
Explicitly model letter–sound correspondence and consonant clusters
Guide short-vowel practice and collect responses
Use decodable reading and spelling/dictation independently

original_guided_practice.prompt: Which element of a structured literacy lesson focused on phonics instruction?
original_guided_practice.feedback_correct: Systematic instruction in letter–sound relationships, decoding, and spelling patterns is central to phonics instruction.
